1	defmodule CleanerCrm.Scheduling do
2	  @moduledoc """
3	  Recurring plans and the jobs they generate, cleaner time-off, and
4	  conflict-aware assignment.
5	
6	  Every function is scoped to the caller's active account.
7	  """
8	
9	  import Ecto.Query, warn: false
10	
11	  alias CleanerCrm.Accounts
12	  alias CleanerCrm.Audit.Recorder
13	  alias CleanerCrm.Repo
14	
15	  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling.{
16	    AvailabilityBlock,
17	    ConflictDetector,
18	    Job,
19	    Recurrence,
20	    RecurringPlan
21	  }
22	
23	  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope
24	  alias CleanerCrm.Users.User
25	
26	  ## Jobs
27	
28	  def get_job!(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, id) when not is_nil(account_id) do
29	    Job
30	    |> where([j], j.account_id == ^account_id)
31	    |> preload([:cleaner, :property, :client])
32	    |> Repo.get!(id)
33	  end
34	
35	  def change_job(%Scope{}, %Job{} = job, attrs \\ %{}) do
36	    Job.changeset(job, attrs)
37	  end
38	
39	  @doc """
40	  Creates a job. Recorded in the audit trail as authored by the
41	  caller, unless `actor: :system` is passed — used when the job is one
42	  occurrence materialized from a recurring plan rather than a job a
43	  human directly asked for (see `create_recurring_plan/2`).
44	  """
45	  def create_job(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, attrs, opts \\ [])
46	      when not is_nil(account_id) do
47	    with {:ok, job} <-
48	           %Job{account_id: account_id}
49	           |> Job.changeset(attrs)
50	           |> Repo.insert() do
51	      record_job_created(scope, job, Keyword.get(opts, :actor, :user))
52	      {:ok, job}
53	    end
54	  end
55	
56	  defp record_job_created(scope, job, :system) do
57	    Recorder.record_system(scope, "job_created", "Job", job.id, %{}, job_created_values(job))
58	  end
59	
60	  defp record_job_created(scope, job, :user) do
61	    Recorder.record(scope, "job_created", "Job", job.id, %{}, job_created_values(job))
62	  end
63	
64	  # Deliberately omits `scheduled_date`: a "created" entry's own
65	  # subject label (job → property/client) is enough to identify which
66	  # job this is, and surfacing it here would read as a schedule change
67	  # (`field_changes/1`'s "Scheduled date: ..." line) indistinguishable
68	  # from an actual reschedule recorded later by `update_job/3`.
69	  defp job_created_values(job) do
70	    %{"cleaner_id" => job.cleaner_id}
71	  end
72	
73	  @doc """
74	  Lists every job scheduled between `week_start` and six days later,
75	  cleaner/property/client preloaded, ordered for the board.
76	  """
77	  def list_jobs_for_week(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, %Date{} = week_start)
78	      when not is_nil(account_id) do
79	    week_end = Date.add(week_start, 6)
80	
81	    Job
82	    |> where(
83	      [j],
84	      j.account_id == ^account_id and j.scheduled_date >= ^week_start and
85	        j.scheduled_date <= ^week_end and j.status != :cancelled
86	    )
87	    |> order_by([j], asc: j.scheduled_date, asc: j.start_time)
88	    |> preload([:cleaner, :property, :client])
89	    |> Repo.all()
90	  end
91	
92	  @doc """
93	  Lists every non-cancelled job for the account, cleaner/property/client
94	  preloaded, ordered for the board. Unlike `list_jobs_for_week/2`, this
95	  isn't bounded to a single week — a recurring plan's series can span
96	  months, and the board needs to account for all of it at a glance.
97	  """

99	    Job
100	    |> where([j], j.account_id == ^account_id and j.status != :cancelled)
101	    |> order_by([j], asc: j.scheduled_date, asc: j.start_time)
102	    |> preload([:cleaner, :property, :client])
103	    |> Repo.all()

defmodule CleanerCrm.Scheduling do
  @moduledoc """
  Recurring plans and the jobs they generate, cleaner time-off, and
  conflict-aware assignment.

  Every function is scoped to the caller's active account.
  """

  import Ecto.Query, warn: false

  alias CleanerCrm.Accounts
  alias CleanerCrm.Audit.Recorder
  alias CleanerCrm.Repo

  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling.{
    AvailabilityBlock,
    ConflictDetector,
    Job,
    Recurrence,
    RecurringPlan
  }

  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.User

  ## Jobs

  def get_job!(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, id) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Job
    |> where([j], j.account_id == ^account_id)
    |> preload([:cleaner, :property, :client])
    |> Repo.get!(id)
  end

  def change_job(%Scope{}, %Job{} = job, attrs \\ %{}) do
    Job.changeset(job, attrs)
  end

  @doc """
  Creates a job. Recorded in the audit trail as authored by the
  caller, unless `actor: :system` is passed — used when the job is one
  occurrence materialized from a recurring plan rather than a job a
  human directly asked for (see `create_recurring_plan/2`).
  """
  def create_job(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, attrs, opts \\ [])
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    with {:ok, job} <-
           %Job{account_id: account_id}
           |> Job.changeset(attrs)
           |> Repo.insert() do
      record_job_created(scope, job, Keyword.get(opts, :actor, :user))
      {:ok, job}
    end
  end

  defp record_job_created(scope, job, :system) do
    Recorder.record_system(scope, "job_created", "Job", job.id, %{}, job_created_values(job))
  end

  defp record_job_created(scope, job, :user) do
    Recorder.record(scope, "job_created", "Job", job.id, %{}, job_created_values(job))
  end

  # Deliberately omits `scheduled_date`: a "created" entry's own
  # subject label (job → property/client) is enough to identify which
  # job this is, and surfacing it here would read as a schedule change
  # (`field_changes/1`'s "Scheduled date: ..." line) indistinguishable
  # from an actual reschedule recorded later by `update_job/3`.
  defp job_created_values(job) do
    %{"cleaner_id" => job.cleaner_id}
  end

  @doc """
  Lists every job scheduled between `week_start` and six days later,
  cleaner/property/client preloaded, ordered for the board.
  """
  def list_jobs_for_week(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, %Date{} = week_start)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    week_end = Date.add(week_start, 6)

    Job
    |> where(
      [j],
      j.account_id == ^account_id and j.scheduled_date >= ^week_start and
        j.scheduled_date <= ^week_end and j.status != :cancelled
    )
    |> order_by([j], asc: j.scheduled_date, asc: j.start_time)
    |> preload([:cleaner, :property, :client])
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  @doc """
  Lists every non-cancelled job for the account, cleaner/property/client
  preloaded, ordered for the board. Unlike `list_jobs_for_week/2`, this
  isn't bounded to a single week — a recurring plan's series can span
  months, and the board needs to account for all of it at a glance.
  """
  def list_jobs(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Job
    |> where([j], j.account_id == ^account_id and j.status != :cancelled)
    |> order_by([j], asc: j.scheduled_date, asc: j.start_time)
    |> preload([:cleaner, :property, :client])
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  @doc """
  Assigns (or reassigns) a job to a cleaner, rejecting the move with
  `{:error, :unavailable}` or `{:error, :overlap}` when it conflicts
  with that cleaner's time off or an existing booking. A `nil`
  `cleaner_id` always succeeds (unassigning never conflicts).
  """
  def assign_cleaner(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, %Job{} = job, cleaner_id)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    with :ok <-
           ConflictDetector.check_assignment(
             scope,
             cleaner_id,
             job.scheduled_date,
             job.start_time,
             job.end_time,
             exclude_job_id: job.id
           ),
         {:ok, updated} <- job |> Job.changeset(%{cleaner_id: cleaner_id}) |> Repo.update() do
      Recorder.record(
        scope,
        "job_reassigned",
        "Job",
        updated.id,
        %{"cleaner_id" => job.cleaner_id},
        %{"cleaner_id" => cleaner_id}
      )

      {:ok, updated}
    end
  end

  def cancel_job(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, %Job{} = job)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    with {:ok, updated} <- job |> Job.changeset(%{status: :cancelled}) |> Repo.update() do
      Recorder.record(
        scope,
        "job_cancelled",
        "Job",
        updated.id,
        %{"status" => to_string(job.status)},
        %{"status" => "cancelled"}
      )

      {:ok, updated}
    end
  end

  @doc """
  Updates a job's schedule and/or price — a reschedule, a price
  change, or both, made directly from the board rather than through
  `assign_cleaner/3`'s conflict-checked path. Records only the fields
  that actually changed to the audit trail, attributed to the caller.
  """
  def update_job(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, %Job{} = job, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    changeset = Job.changeset(job, attrs)

    with {:ok, updated} <- Repo.update(changeset) do
      record_job_updated(scope, job, changeset, updated)
      {:ok, updated}
    end
  end

  @audited_update_fields ~w(scheduled_date start_time end_time agreed_price_cents status)a

  defp record_job_updated(scope, job, changeset, updated) do
    changed_fields =
      changeset.changes
      |> Map.keys()
      |> Enum.filter(&(&1 in @audited_update_fields))

    if changed_fields != [] do
      Recorder.record(
        scope,
        update_action(changed_fields),
        "Job",
        updated.id,
        audit_snapshot(job, changed_fields),
        audit_snapshot(updated, changed_fields)
      )
    end
  end

  defp update_action(changed_fields) do
    cond do
      Enum.any?(changed_fields, &(&1 in [:scheduled_date, :start_time, :end_time])) ->
        "job_rescheduled"

      :agreed_price_cents in changed_fields ->
        "job_price_changed"

      true ->
        "job_updated"
    end
  end

  defp audit_snapshot(job, fields),
    do: Map.new(fields, &{to_string(&1), audit_value(Map.get(job, &1))})

  defp audit_value(%Date{} = value), do: to_string(value)
  defp audit_value(%Time{} = value), do: to_string(value)
  defp audit_value(value), do: value

  @doc """
  Removes a job from the board without hard-deleting its row — the
  row (and any audit entries already about it) stays resolvable for
  the trail. Distinct from `cancel_job/2`: this is the office
  correcting a mistaken entry rather than calling off an appointment,
  so it's recorded as "deleted" rather than "cancelled" and never
  notifies the assigned cleaner.
  """
  def delete_job(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, %Job{} = job)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    with {:ok, updated} <- job |> Job.changeset(%{status: :cancelled}) |> Repo.update() do
      Recorder.record(
        scope,
        "job_deleted",
        "Job",
        updated.id,
        %{"status" => to_string(job.status)},
        %{"status" => "cancelled"}
      )

      {:ok, updated}
    end
  end

  ## Recurring plans

  def get_recurring_plan!(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, id)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    RecurringPlan
    |> where([p], p.account_id == ^account_id)
    |> preload([:property, :cleaner])
    |> Repo.get!(id)
  end

  def change_recurring_plan(%Scope{}, %RecurringPlan{} = plan, attrs \\ %{}) do
    RecurringPlan.preview_changeset(plan, attrs)
  end

  @doc """
  Runs conflict detection for a (possibly unsaved) plan's full series
  against its preferred cleaner, without persisting anything. Returns
  only the conflicting occurrences, as `[%{index:, date:, reason:}]`.
  """
  def preview_conflicts(scope, %RecurringPlan{} = plan) do
    ConflictDetector.check_occurrences(scope, plan, Recurrence.occurrences(plan))
  end

  @doc """
  Saves a recurring plan and materializes its full series of jobs.
  Conflicting occurrences are still created and still assigned to the
  preferred cleaner — conflicts are for the owner to review and
  resolve, never a silent block on saving.
  """
  def create_recurring_plan(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Repo.transact(fn ->
      with {:ok, plan} <-
             %RecurringPlan{account_id: account_id}
             |> RecurringPlan.changeset(attrs)
             |> Repo.insert() do
        jobs =
          plan
          |> Recurrence.job_attrs()
          |> Enum.map(fn job_attrs ->
            {:ok, job} = create_job(scope, job_attrs, actor: :system)
            job
          end)

        {:ok, {plan, jobs}}
      end
    end)
  end

  ## Availability blocks

  def change_availability_block(%Scope{}, %AvailabilityBlock{} = block, attrs \\ %{}) do
    AvailabilityBlock.changeset(block, attrs)
  end

  def create_availability_block(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    %AvailabilityBlock{account_id: account_id}
    |> AvailabilityBlock.changeset(attrs)
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  ## Cleaners (account members who take jobs)

  @doc """
  Lists the account's members as candidate cleaners for the board and
  assignment pickers.
  """
  def list_cleaners(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    scope
    |> Accounts.list_account_members(account_id)
    |> Enum.map(& &1.user)
  end

  @doc """
  Registers a new cleaner: a user identified by display name (rather
  than login credentials) added to the account as a member, so jobs
  and availability can be assigned to them. There is no login flow for
  a cleaner created this way — see `CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures.cleaner_fixture/3`
  for the (real, login-capable) path other stories seed cleaners
  through.
  """
  def register_cleaner(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, name)
      when not is_nil(account_id) and is_binary(name) do
    with {:ok, user} <- insert_cleaner_user(name),
         {:ok, _member} <- Accounts.add_user_to_account(scope, user.id, account_id, :member) do
      {:ok, user}
    end
  end

  @doc """
  Fetches a single cleaner by id, for their detail page. Draws from
  the same membership list as `list_cleaners/1`, so a user who isn't
  a member of this account can't be looked up here either. Raises if
  not found.
  """
  def get_cleaner!(%Scope{} = scope, id) do
    cleaner_id = parse_cleaner_id(id)

    scope
    |> list_cleaners()
    |> Enum.find(&(&1.id == cleaner_id))
    |> case do
      nil -> raise Ecto.NoResultsError, queryable: User
      cleaner -> cleaner
    end
  end

  @doc """
  Lists a cleaner's time-off blocks for their detail page, soonest
  first.
  """

      when not is_nil(account_id) do

    AvailabilityBlock
    |> where([b], b.account_id == ^account_id and b.cleaner_id == ^cleaner_id)
    |> order_by([b], asc: b.date)
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  @doc """
  Lists a cleaner's upcoming (today or later, non-cancelled) jobs for
  their detail page, soonest first.
  """

      when not is_nil(account_id) do

    Job
    |> where(
      [j],
      j.account_id == ^account_id and j.cleaner_id == ^cleaner_id and
        j.status != :cancelled and j.scheduled_date >= ^Date.utc_today()
    )
    |> order_by([j], asc: j.scheduled_date, asc: j.start_time)
    |> preload([:property, :client])
    |> Repo.all()

  defp parse_cleaner_id(id) when is_integer(id), do: id
  defp parse_cleaner_id(id) when is_binary(id), do: String.to_integer(id)

2	  @moduledoc """
3	  Room-by-room checklists instantiated per job, before/after photo
4	  proof, incident reports (damage, missing items, unsafe conditions),
5	  and the scorecards that aggregate a cleaner's completed jobs.
6	
7	  Every function is scoped to the caller's active account.
8	  """
9	
10	  import Ecto.Query, warn: false

24	  }
25	
26	  ## Checklist templates
27	
28	  def list_checklist_templates(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id})
29	      when not is_nil(account_id) do
30	    ChecklistTemplate
31	    |> where([t], t.account_id == ^account_id)
32	    |> order_by([t], asc: t.name)
33	    |> Repo.all()
34	  end
35	
36	  def get_checklist_template!(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, id)
37	      when not is_nil(account_id) do
38	    ChecklistTemplate
39	    |> where([t], t.account_id == ^account_id)
40	    |> Repo.get!(id)
41	  end
42	
43	  def change_checklist_template(%Scope{}, %ChecklistTemplate{} = template, attrs \\ %{}) do
44	    ChecklistTemplate.changeset(template, attrs)
45	  end
46	
47	  def create_checklist_template(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, attrs)
48	      when not is_nil(account_id) do
49	    %ChecklistTemplate{account_id: account_id}
50	    |> ChecklistTemplate.changeset(attrs)
51	    |> Repo.insert()
52	  end
53	
54	  ## Checklists
55	
56	  @doc """
57	  Instantiates a job's checklist from a template, copying its
58	  room/task/required lines down as the job's own checklist items.
59	  """
60	  def instantiate_checklist(%Scope{} = scope, %Job{} = job, %ChecklistTemplate{} = template) do
61	    create_checklist(scope, job, ChecklistTemplate.item_attrs(template), template_id: template.id)
62	  end
63	
64	  @doc """
65	  Creates a job's checklist from `items` — each a `%{task:, required:}`
66	  map, optionally carrying `room:` — in the order given. Every
67	  checklist item starts unchecked and un-skipped.
68	  """
69	  def create_checklist(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, %Job{id: job_id}, items, opts \\ [])
70	      when not is_nil(account_id) and is_list(items) do
71	    Repo.transact(fn ->
72	      with {:ok, checklist} <-
73	             %Checklist{account_id: account_id}
74	             |> Checklist.changeset(%{job_id: job_id, checklist_template_id: opts[:template_id]})
75	             |> Repo.insert() do
76	        item_structs =
77	          items
78	          |> Enum.with_index()
79	          |> Enum.map(fn {attrs, position} ->
80	            insert_checklist_item!(checklist, attrs, position)
81	          end)
82	
83	        {:ok, %{checklist | items: item_structs}}
84	      end
85	    end)
86	  end
87	
88	  defp insert_checklist_item!(checklist, attrs, position) do
89	    params =
90	      attrs
91	      |> Map.new(fn {key, value} -> {to_string(key), value} end)
92	      |> Map.put("checklist_id", checklist.id)
93	      |> Map.put_new("position", position)
94	
95	    %ChecklistItem{}
96	    |> ChecklistItem.changeset(params)
97	    |> Repo.insert!()
98	  end
99	
100	  @doc """
101	  Fetches a job's checklist with its items and their photos
102	  preloaded, or `nil` if the job has none yet.
103	  """
104	  def get_checklist_for_job(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, %Job{id: job_id})

defmodule CleanerCrm.Quality do
  @moduledoc """
  Room-by-room checklists instantiated per job, before/after photo
  proof, incident reports (damage, missing items, unsafe conditions),
  and the scorecards that aggregate a cleaner's completed jobs.

  Every function is scoped to the caller's active account.
  """

  import Ecto.Query, warn: false

  alias CleanerCrm.Audit.Recorder
  alias CleanerCrm.Repo
  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Job
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope

  alias CleanerCrm.Quality.{
    Checklist,
    ChecklistItem,
    ChecklistTemplate,
    IncidentReport,
    Photo,
    Scorecard
  }

  ## Checklist templates

  def list_checklist_templates(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id})
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    ChecklistTemplate
    |> where([t], t.account_id == ^account_id)
    |> order_by([t], asc: t.name)
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  def get_checklist_template!(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, id)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    ChecklistTemplate
    |> where([t], t.account_id == ^account_id)
    |> Repo.get!(id)
  end

  def change_checklist_template(%Scope{}, %ChecklistTemplate{} = template, attrs \\ %{}) do
    ChecklistTemplate.changeset(template, attrs)
  end

  def create_checklist_template(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    %ChecklistTemplate{account_id: account_id}
    |> ChecklistTemplate.changeset(attrs)
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  ## Checklists

  @doc """
  Instantiates a job's checklist from a template, copying its
  room/task/required lines down as the job's own checklist items.
  """
  def instantiate_checklist(%Scope{} = scope, %Job{} = job, %ChecklistTemplate{} = template) do
    create_checklist(scope, job, ChecklistTemplate.item_attrs(template), template_id: template.id)
  end

  @doc """
  Creates a job's checklist from `items` — each a `%{task:, required:}`
  map, optionally carrying `room:` — in the order given. Every
  checklist item starts unchecked and un-skipped.
  """
  def create_checklist(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, %Job{id: job_id}, items, opts \\ [])
      when not is_nil(account_id) and is_list(items) do
    Repo.transact(fn ->
      with {:ok, checklist} <-
             %Checklist{account_id: account_id}
             |> Checklist.changeset(%{job_id: job_id, checklist_template_id: opts[:template_id]})
             |> Repo.insert() do
        item_structs =
          items
          |> Enum.with_index()
          |> Enum.map(fn {attrs, position} ->
            insert_checklist_item!(checklist, attrs, position)
          end)

        {:ok, %{checklist | items: item_structs}}
      end
    end)
  end

  defp insert_checklist_item!(checklist, attrs, position) do
    params =
      attrs
      |> Map.new(fn {key, value} -> {to_string(key), value} end)
      |> Map.put("checklist_id", checklist.id)
      |> Map.put_new("position", position)

    %ChecklistItem{}
    |> ChecklistItem.changeset(params)
    |> Repo.insert!()
  end

  @doc """
  Fetches a job's checklist with its items and their photos
  preloaded, or `nil` if the job has none yet.
  """
  def get_checklist_for_job(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, %Job{id: job_id})
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Checklist
    |> where([c], c.account_id == ^account_id and c.job_id == ^job_id)
    |> preload(items: :photos)
    |> Repo.one()
  end

  @doc """
  Groups a checklist's items by room, in the order each room first
  appears. Items with no room (a flat, unrouted checklist) are
  grouped under `nil`.
  """
  def group_by_room(%Checklist{items: items}) do
    rooms = Enum.uniq_by(items, & &1.room) |> Enum.map(& &1.room)
    grouped = Enum.group_by(items, & &1.room)
    Enum.map(rooms, &{&1, Map.fetch!(grouped, &1)})
  end

  @doc "`{checked_count, total_count}` across a checklist's items."
  def progress(%Checklist{items: items}), do: {Enum.count(items, & &1.checked), length(items)}

  @doc """
  Toggles a checklist item's checked state. Checking an item clears
  any prior skip.
  """
  def toggle_checklist_item(%Scope{}, %ChecklistItem{checked: true} = item) do
    item |> ChecklistItem.uncheck_changeset() |> Repo.update()
  end

  def toggle_checklist_item(%Scope{}, %ChecklistItem{} = item) do
    item |> ChecklistItem.check_changeset() |> Repo.update()
  end

  @doc "Marks a required item skipped instead of done, with a reason."
  def skip_checklist_item(%Scope{}, %ChecklistItem{} = item, reason) do
    item |> ChecklistItem.skip_changeset(reason) |> Repo.update()
  end

  @doc """
  The required items still blocking completion: unchecked and not
  skipped. Empty means the checklist is ready to complete.
  """
  def incomplete_required_items(%Checklist{items: items}) do
    Enum.filter(items, &(&1.required and not &1.checked and not &1.skipped))
  end

  @doc """
  Completes a job's checklist: refused with the still-incomplete
  required items when any remain; otherwise the checklist is stamped
  done, scored, and the job itself is marked completed.
  """
  def complete_job(%Scope{} = scope, %Checklist{} = checklist) do
    case incomplete_required_items(checklist) do
      [] -> do_complete_job(scope, checklist)
      incomplete -> {:error, {:incomplete_required_tasks, incomplete}}
    end
  end

  defp do_complete_job(scope, checklist) do
    Repo.transact(fn ->
      with {:ok, completed} <- mark_checklist_completed(checklist),
           {:ok, _job} <- mark_job_completed(scope, completed.job_id) do
        {:ok, completed}
      end
    end)
  end

  defp mark_checklist_completed(checklist) do
    checklist
    |> Checklist.changeset(%{
      completed_at: DateTime.utc_now(),
      quality_score: Scorecard.score(checklist)
    })
    |> Repo.update()
  end

  defp mark_job_completed(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, job_id) do
    job = Job |> where([j], j.account_id == ^account_id) |> Repo.get!(job_id)

    with {:ok, updated} <- job |> Job.changeset(%{status: :completed}) |> Repo.update() do
      Recorder.record(
        scope,
        "job_completed",
        "Job",
        updated.id,
        %{"status" => to_string(job.status)},
        %{"status" => "completed"}
      )

      {:ok, updated}
    end
  end

  @doc """
  Records the owner's 1-5 quality rating for a job, recomputing the
  checklist's combined quality score.
  """
  def rate_job(%Scope{}, %Checklist{} = checklist, rating) do
    rated = %{checklist | owner_rating: rating}

    checklist
    |> Checklist.changeset(%{owner_rating: rating, quality_score: Scorecard.score(rated)})
    |> Repo.update()
  end

  @doc """
  Creates a job's checklist already fully checked off with
  before/after photo proof, for callers that seed a completed job's
  proof of work directly (see
  `CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures.job_with_proof_of_work_fixture/3`) rather
  than driving the checklist item by item. `items` is a list of
  `%{task:, before_photo:, after_photo:}` maps.
  """
  def complete_checklist(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, %Job{} = job, items)
      when not is_nil(account_id) and is_list(items) do
    Repo.transact(fn ->
      with {:ok, checklist} <-
             create_checklist(
               scope,
               job,
               Enum.map(items, &Map.take(&1, [:task, :room, :required]))
             ) do
        checked_items =
          checklist.items
          |> Enum.zip(items)
          |> Enum.map(fn {item, proof} -> check_with_photos!(account_id, item, proof) end)

        checklist = %{checklist | items: checked_items}

        checklist
        |> Checklist.changeset(%{
          completed_at: DateTime.utc_now(),
          quality_score: Scorecard.score(checklist)
        })
        |> Repo.update()
      end
    end)
  end

  defp check_with_photos!(account_id, item, %{
         before_photo: before_photo,
         after_photo: after_photo
       }) do
    checked = item |> ChecklistItem.check_changeset() |> Repo.update!()
    before = insert_checklist_photo!(account_id, checked, :before, before_photo)
    aftr = insert_checklist_photo!(account_id, checked, :after, after_photo)
    %{checked | photos: [before, aftr]}
  end

  defp insert_checklist_photo!(account_id, %ChecklistItem{} = item, kind, storage_key) do
    %Photo{account_id: account_id}
    |> Photo.changeset(%{
      checklist_item_id: item.id,
      kind: kind,
      upload_state: :uploaded,
      storage_key: storage_key,
      captured_at: DateTime.utc_now()
    })
    |> Repo.insert!()
  end

  @doc "Attaches a before/after photo to a checklist item, `:pending` until uploaded."
  def attach_photo(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, %ChecklistItem{} = item, kind, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) and kind in [:before, :after] do
    %Photo{account_id: account_id}
    |> Photo.changeset(Map.merge(%{checklist_item_id: item.id, kind: kind}, attrs))
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  @doc "Flips a pending photo to uploaded once its bytes land in storage."
  def complete_photo_upload(%Scope{}, %Photo{} = photo, storage_key) do
    photo |> Photo.uploaded_changeset(storage_key) |> Repo.update()
  end

  ## Incident reports

  @doc """
  Files an incident report for a job. `attrs` needs `:type`
  (`"damage"`, `"missing_item"`, or `"unsafe_condition"`) and
  `:description`; a `:photo` (the same attrs `attach_photo/4` takes)
  is required unless `:type` is `"unsafe_condition"`. The cleaner and
  filing time are always the caller's and now — never accepted from
  `attrs` — and nothing about a filed report can change afterward.
  """
  def file_incident_report(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id, user: user}, %Job{} = job, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    {photo_attrs, report_attrs} = attrs |> stringify_keys() |> Map.pop("photo")

    Repo.transact(fn ->
      with {:ok, report} <-
             %IncidentReport{account_id: account_id}
             |> IncidentReport.changeset(
               Map.merge(report_attrs, %{
                 "job_id" => job.id,
                 "cleaner_id" => user && user.id,
                 "filed_at" => DateTime.utc_now()
               }),
               not is_nil(photo_attrs)
             )
             |> Repo.insert() do
        photo = photo_attrs && insert_incident_photo!(account_id, report, photo_attrs)
        {:ok, %{report | photos: Enum.filter([photo], & &1)}}
      end
    end)
  end

  defp stringify_keys(attrs), do: Map.new(attrs, fn {key, value} -> {to_string(key), value} end)

  defp insert_incident_photo!(account_id, %IncidentReport{} = report, photo_attrs) do
    %Photo{account_id: account_id}
    |> Photo.changeset(
      Map.merge(stringify_keys(photo_attrs), %{
        "incident_report_id" => report.id,
        "kind" => "incident",
        "upload_state" => "uploaded",
        "captured_at" => DateTime.utc_now()
      })
    )
    |> Repo.insert!()
  end

  @doc """
  Lists an account's incident reports, most recently filed first,
  with job (and its client), cleaner, and photos preloaded.
  """
  def list_incident_reports(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    IncidentReport
    |> where([r], r.account_id == ^account_id)
    |> order_by([r], desc: r.filed_at)
    |> preload([:cleaner, :photos, job: [:client, :property]])
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  ## Scorecards

  @doc """
  The cleaner's average quality score and trend across their
  completed jobs, oldest first (see `CleanerCrm.Quality.Scorecard`).
  """
  def cleaner_scorecard(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, cleaner_id)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Checklist
    |> join(:inner, [c], j in Job, on: j.id == c.job_id)
    |> where(
      [c, j],
      c.account_id == ^account_id and j.cleaner_id == ^cleaner_id and
        not is_nil(c.completed_at)
    )
    |> order_by([c], asc: c.completed_at)
    |> select([c], c.quality_score)
    |> Repo.all()
    |> Enum.reject(&is_nil/1)
    |> Scorecard.aggregate()
  end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Quality.ChecklistTemplate do
  @moduledoc """
  A reusable room-by-room task template for a property or service
  type, from which a job's own `CleanerCrm.Quality.Checklist` can be
  instantiated (see `CleanerCrm.Quality.instantiate_checklist/3`).
  """

  use Ecto.Schema
  import Ecto.Changeset

  defmodule TemplateItem do
    @moduledoc """
    One room/task line on a template, embedded — a template is a
    small, template-owned list, not something referenced elsewhere,
    so it lives inline rather than as its own table.
    """

    use Ecto.Schema
    import Ecto.Changeset

    @type t :: %__MODULE__{
            room: String.t() | nil,
            task: String.t() | nil,
            required: boolean()
          }

    @primary_key false
    embedded_schema do
      field :room, :string
      field :task, :string
      field :required, :boolean, default: true
    end

    def changeset(item, attrs) do
      item
      |> cast(attrs, [:room, :task, :required])
      |> validate_required([:task])
    end
  end

  @type t :: %__MODULE__{
          id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          account_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          property_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          name: String.t() | nil,
          items: [TemplateItem.t()],
          inserted_at: DateTime.t() | nil,
          updated_at: DateTime.t() | nil
        }

  @primary_key {:id, :binary_id, autogenerate: true}
  schema "checklist_templates" do
    field :name, :string
    embeds_many :items, TemplateItem, on_replace: :delete

    belongs_to :account, CleanerCrm.Accounts.Account, type: :binary_id
    belongs_to :property, CleanerCrm.Clients.Property, type: :binary_id

    timestamps(type: :utc_datetime_usec)
  end

  def changeset(template, attrs) do
    template
    |> cast(attrs, [:name, :property_id])
    |> cast_embed(:items, with: &TemplateItem.changeset/2)
    |> validate_required([:name])
  end

  @doc """
  This template's items as the flat `%{room:, task:, required:}` maps
  `CleanerCrm.Quality.create_checklist/4` expects.
  """
  def item_attrs(%__MODULE__{items: items}) do
    Enum.map(items, &Map.take(&1, [:room, :task, :required]))
  end
end
